Question: What is the boiling point of water at the top of Everest?

The boiling point of water at the top of Mount Everest is approximately **70°C (158°F)**. This is significantly lower than the standard boiling point of 100°C (212°F) at sea level, due to the much lower atmospheric pressure at Everest's summit (around 33.7 kPa or about one-third of sea-level pressure).
